title: Fail fast on missing key.properties instead of silently debug-signing release Android builds (build.gradle.kts)
rule: Tier-2 area note (security) — AG-11-adjacent CI guardrail soft-skip
why: When KEYSTORE_BASE64 is unset (misconfigured secret, or a maintainer manually dispatches the 'Build APK' workflow with build_type=release before secrets are wired up), build.yml prints a warning but does not fail — it proceeds to 'flutter build apk --release'. Because key.properties was never written, Gradle's fallback here silently signs the 'release' APK with the shared, publicly-known Flutter debug keystore, then uploads it as a GitHub Actions artifact literally named learning-tracker-release-apk. Anyone who installs that artifact believing it's a genuine release build gets a debug-signed binary; since the debug key is identical across virtually all Flutter/Android-Studio installs, another developer's debug-signed build could later 'update' over it without Android's signature check objecting.
recommendation: Make the release signingConfig fail fast (e.g. error("release build requested but key.properties is missing")) instead of silently substituting debug signing, or at minimum have build.yml's keystore-decode step exit 1 when build_type == 'release' and the secret is empty instead of only warning.
acceptance_criteria: flutter build apk --release (or ./gradlew assembleRelease) fails loudly when key.properties/keystore secret is absent, instead of producing a debug-signed 'release' artifact.
build.yml's release job aborts (non-zero exit) when KEYSTORE_BASE64 is empty and build_type=release.

corrections: docs/deployment-guide.md:25 documents the debug-signing fallback as intentional design ('falls back to debug signing if absent'), undercutting the 'silently' framing and the primary fail-hard-Gradle recommendation, which would break the documented local-dev flow. The 'debug key identical across installs' claim is also a common misconception: no shared debug.keystore is committed in this repo, and each machine/CI run auto-generates its own unique debug key, so there's no real cross-device signature-collision/update risk as described. The narrower, still-valid residual issue is that build.yml doesn't fail-fast when an explicit release dispatch is missing its secret, silently uploading a mislabeled artifact.
